interface.signature: def biGraph(n: int, e: int, arr: list[int]) -> int:

preconditions.expression: n >= 2 and e >= 1 and e <= 100 and n <= 100 and len(arr) == 2 * e
preconditions.description: The graph has at least 2 vertices and at least 1 edge, with n and e within constraints, and arr contains exactly 2*e integers representing undirected edges (each edge listed twice, once in each direction).

preconditions.expression: all(0 <= u < n and 0 <= v < n for u, v in zip(arr[::2], arr[1::2]))
preconditions.description: Every edge in arr connects two vertices u and v where 0 ≤ u, v < n.

postconditions.expression: return_value == 1 if (all(len(neighbors) >= 2 for neighbors in [set() for _ in range(n)] if (u := arr[i], v := arr[i+1]) and (neighbors[u].add(v) or neighbors[v].add(u)) for i in range(0, len(arr), 2)) and any(neighbors[u] for u in range(n)) and (not any(len(neighbors[u]) == 1 for u in range(n)) or n == 2)) else 0
postconditions.description: The graph is biconnected (return_value = 1) if and only if it is connected and has no articulation points (vertices whose removal disconnects the graph). For n=2, the graph is trivially biconnected if there is an edge.

postconditions.expression: return_value == 0 if (any(len(neighbors[u]) == 0 for u in range(n)) or any(len(neighbors[u]) == 1 for u in range(n)) if n > 2) else 1
postconditions.description: The graph is not biconnected (return_value = 0) if it is disconnected (a vertex with no edges) or has a leaf node (a vertex with only one edge) unless n=2.
